status_summary: After the Commission regained a quorum in late 2025 (per law-firm commentary), the EEOC votes page records a 2-1 vote on 2026-01-21 approving a resolution concerning the Commission's authority to commence or intervene in litigation; the resolution text, signed 2026-01-22, makes the decision to file or intervene in litigation a majority vote of the Commission, with vote periods of 5 or 7 business days, and leaves enforcement of consent decrees and settlements, recordkeeping enforcement and some other matters delegated to the General Counsel. On 2026-01-22 the Commission voted 2-1 to rescind its 2024 harassment enforcement guidance. A 2026-01-14 vote giving the Chair agenda control was reported only by a law firm. No disclaimer of consent-decree power or of rulemaking authority, and no reorientation toward disability and pregnancy accommodation claims, was found.

timeline.event: The Commission voted 2-1 on a resolution concerning its authority to commence or intervene in litigation; the resolution text (signed 2026-01-22) returns most litigation decisions to a majority vote of the Commission, with vote deadlines of 5 or 7 business days, and leaves consent decree enforcement and some other matters with the General Counsel.
The Commission voted 2-1 to rescind its 2024 Enforcement Guidance on Harassment in the Workplace.

title: EEOC governance reforms: Commission votes, guidance rescission, enforcement priorities
uncertainties: The quorum restoration and the 2026-01-14 agenda vote come from law-firm commentary, which gives no exact quorum date; the EEOC votes page for January 2026 lists a 2-1 resolution of 2026-01-13 on Chair and Commission roles regarding agency organizational changes but no 2026-01-14 entry, so the two may be the same action; the 2026-01-13 resolution text was not opened. The resolution on litigation authority carries a signature date of 2026-01-22 and no vote date, while the votes page lists the final vote on 2026-01-21; the timeline dates the event by the vote. The resolution applies a majority-vote rule to decisions to file or intervene but keeps enforcement of consent decrees and settlements with the General Counsel and does not disclaim authority to enter consent decrees; it does not mention rulemaking. The harassment rescission release gives no reasons and mentions no rulemaking or consent decrees. Later months of votes were not reviewed. The 2026-05-07 release is the agency's own characterization of its work, was not re-read in this pass, and is not treated as an event.
